sections.title: Aldous' spectral gap phenomena in stochastic exchange models
sections.abstract: The authors prove that a broad class of conservative exchange models has a spectral gap attained by an observable of degree at most two, settling a recent Alon–Puder conjecture and identifying when one- versus two-particle modes dominate.
sections.claimed_result: The spectral gap is always realized by a polynomial of degree at most two in the energy variables, with a geometry-dependent one- versus two-particle transition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Conservative continuous-spin systems on weighted graphs or hypergraphs with Dirichlet reversible measures; boundary-driven variants are treated separately.
sections.caveat: New unrefereed 75-page preprint; extensive claims require technical verification.

sections.title: Superpolynomial lower bounds for vertex numbers of real projective space triangulations via a topological Figiel-Lindenstrauss-Milman theorem
sections.abstract: Every simplicial triangulation of real projective d-space has exp(Omega(sqrt(d))) vertices, determining the minimum vertex number up to exp(d^(1/2+o(1))).
sections.claimed_result: The minimum number of vertices in a triangulation of real projective d-space satisfies mu_d = exp(d^(1/2+o(1))).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Simplicial triangulations and finite strongly regular CW complexes with free cellular involution; applications include topological graph coloring and sign complexes.
sections.caveat: The new topological inequality and its applications need expert verification.

sections.title: Pierce-Birkhoff conjecture is false
sections.abstract: The authors give a counterexample to the Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture: a continuous function piecewise quadratic on finitely many semialgebraic sets that is not a finite lattice combination of polynomials.
sections.claimed_result: A continuous piecewise-quadratic semialgebraic function is exhibited that contradicts the Pierce–Birkhoff conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Functions on R^n, finite semialgebraic partitions, piecewise quadratic data, and lattice combinations of polynomials.
sections.caveat: A conjecture-disproof claim requires careful independent checking of the example and quantifiers.

sections.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
sections.abstract: The authors claim the sharp Hausdorff–Young inequality on quantum Euclidean space and sharp constants for the Weyl transform and Heisenberg group.
sections.claimed_result: Sharp Hausdorff–Young constants are obtained for quantum Euclidean space, the Weyl transform, and the Heisenberg group.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Quantum Euclidean space and noncommutative convolution; the proof uses an operator-valued flow related to the Gabor transform.
sections.caveat: The authors explicitly call the manuscript rough and promise a polished update.

sections.title: From Nilspace Theory to Simplicial Homotopy Theory
sections.abstract: The paper constructs a faithful functor from cubespaces to condensed simplicial sets, translating nilspace structure into a Postnikov tower and identifying structure groups with simplicial homotopy groups.
sections.claimed_result: Nilspaces map to Kan complexes, with structure groups corresponding to simplicial homotopy groups.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Categories of cubespaces, nilspaces, condensed simplicial sets, and a specially constructed cosimplicial cubical set.
sections.caveat: The abstract does not establish computational effectiveness or preservation of all structures relevant to applications.
